methodological_questions: Can a teammate's similarity to the absent player's pre-absence initiation profile (or minutes / same-position minutes) predict who gains most in the absent player's primary play types?
Is 11 cases (148 spells, non-independent within case) enough power for a test of the closest-profile gainer claim?
Can profile similarity be measured without using post-absence outcomes (outcome leakage)?
Do injury type, role change, and regression to the mean confound attribution of post-absence gains?

historical_evidence.finding: Closest prior study of this concept (play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade). Mean similarity was +0.863 for ABSORBED vs +0.848 for CASCADE, and Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19, recorded as wrong-signed. Similarity did not separate absorption from cascade and was almost always findable. Recorded failure mechanism: B_powered_null. Sample and power were NOT_RECORDED; validation was no_validation_recorded.

Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, n=96 matched pairs; n=25 vs terminal). Excludes organizers from the licensed comparison. Relevant to absence-driven reorganization, but it tests team identity, not the closest-profile teammate gain.

Post-hoc matched-pair test of adapt vs continue after a suppressed play type. Group B (n=255 pairs, 242 games at caliper 0.10) was a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, and its CI included 0 (p=0.386). Recorded failure mechanism: A_unanswerable.

Holdout play-type ranking from training data correlated with held-out efficiency (median rho +0.539; 10.5% of rows had rho<0). Doc caveat: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types. Relevant only as a caution about play-type labels and league-wide effects.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap of +0.427 in the same direction as the team gap, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. Relevant as a caution about per-player sample size.

Exploratory player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 gaps across 78 players with min 5 rows per tier. Results were mixed in sign and n was small for most players. Relevant as a caution about per-player gaps on single-game data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type/initiation similarity to separate absorbed from cascaded play-type volume after a player's absence.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null with the similarity signal wrong-signed (Spearman -0.19). Recorded limit: LIM:label_or_classification_error (RISK:LABEL_ERROR). Power was not recorded, so the null cannot be assumed to be well-powered.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Per-player gap estimation from small single-game play-type samples.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE; n was small for most players, and no multiplicity or clustered test was run.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Post-hoc comparison of successful vs unsuccessful adaptation cohorts.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: the Group B cohort was reconstructed post hoc, not validated, and the caliper-0.10 CI included 0.

evidence_establishes: Similarity-based replacement identification did not separate absorption from cascade in the closest prior study (SF-CHT-052), and its direction was wrong-signed.
Per-player and post-hoc cohort analyses in this project have repeatedly been underpowered or unanswerable at the player level (SF-APPA-048, SF-APPS-025, SF-APPS-036).
Absence-related team identity effects have been detected with large matched samples (SF-APPS-088, n=96 pairs), so absence analysis is feasible when the sample is much larger than 11 cases.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the specific claim that the closest pre-absence-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
No retrieved record reports the power or sample size of SF-CHT-052, so its null cannot be taken as a powered negative result for this question.
Nothing retrieved shows how many of the 11 cases have usable pre-absence and post-absence initiation data, or how injury type and role change affect them.
own_inferences: With 11 cases, even a true effect would be hard to distinguish from noise. The 148 spells are repeated observations within those cases, not 148 independent units.

The closest-profile definition depends on a choice of similarity metric (initiation share, total minutes, or same-position minutes), and each choice may produce a different gainer. Choosing the metric after seeing outcomes would be a forking-paths problem.
Defining 'primary types' from the absent player's own pre-absence usage and then measuring gains on the same play-type possessions may build the outcome into the label.
Regression to the mean is likely: the teammate with the largest post-absence gain may simply be the one whose baseline was lowest.
uncertainties: Power and sample details for SF-CHT-052 were NOT_RECORDED.

Whether the 2025-26 regular season data (complete from 2026-04-13) and the partial 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21) are used matters for the 11-case count. This could change if partial playoff files are included.
The retrieved set has no record of play-type classification reliability for the play-by-play derived types.
No prior record defines how absence cases were selected (injury vs rest vs trade), so the 11-case set may be selected on post-absence outcomes.

historical_effect.explanation: The closest prior study (SF-CHT-052) found that similarity did not separate absorption from cascade and was wrong-signed. That lowers the prior that profile similarity will predict the largest gainer. Combined with the 11-case sample and the player-level underpowering in SF-APPA-048 and SF-APPS-025, the evidence points toward not running the question as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 absence cases give too few independent units for a reliable test of who gains most; 148 spells are clustered within cases.
Initiation-profile similarity and play-type classification may be unreliable, as the SF-CHT-052 label-error caveat suggests.
Defining primary types and measuring gains on the same possessions can build the outcome into the label.
Injury type, role change, and minute changes after absence can produce gains unrelated to profile similarity.
The largest gainer may be the teammate with the lowest baseline, so the gain could be regression to the mean.

prior_work.summary: The closest prior study (SF-CHT-052) tested similarity-based replacement vs absorb/cascade and found no separation, with the wrong-signed effect recorded as B_powered_null but with power NOT_RECORDED. SF-APPS-088 showed that absence effects on team identity are detectable with large matched samples but does not address the closest-profile teammate. No retrieved study directly tests the closest-profile gainer claim, so the question is only partly addressed.

risks.text: 11 cases, with 148 non-independent spells, gives very low power to detect the closest-profile gainer effect.
Play-type and initiator labels derived from play-by-play may misclassify possessions, as recorded for SF-CHT-052.
Profile similarity depends on the chosen metric (initiation share, minutes, or same-position minutes), and results may vary across metrics.
Primary play types defined from the same post-absence data used to measure gains would make the test circular.
Using post-absence information to choose the closest-profile teammate would leak outcome information into the predictor.
Gainers chosen by largest post-absence change are likely to be selected partly by noise and regression to the mean.
Injury type, role change, and simultaneous roster moves can drive redistribution independently of profile similarity.
Several similarity metrics and play-type definitions would multiply the chance of a spurious significant result.
Per-player gap analyses in prior work (SF-APPA-048) were small-n and not clustered, and placebo checks are not specified here.

design.estimand: Minimum viable: descriptive per-case pattern of which teammate gains most in the absent player's primary play types, and whether the closest-profile teammate is among them. No causal or confirmatory claim.
design.unit: Absence case (player-absence event), with spells as nested observations.
design.sample: The 11 cases as recorded, using only cases with pre-absence and post-absence play-by-play available from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons. Exclude partial 2025-26 playoff files before 2026-06-21.
design.power: Not powered for inference at n=11. Report descriptively with per-case intervals only. Any confirmatory test would need a substantially larger set of absence events, not available here.
design.controls: Pre-register the similarity metric (initiation share, primary) and the primary-type definition from pre-absence data only. Adjust for injury type, minutes change, and roster changes. Use a regression-to-the-mean baseline (e.g., the teammate's pre-absence rate vs a matched non-absence window).
design.falsification: The claim fails if the closest-profile teammate is not the largest gainer in most cases and the wrong-signed pattern from SF-CHT-052 persists in the descriptive comparison.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary metric and play-type definition. Alternate metrics (minutes, same-position minutes) reported as secondary descriptive results with a correction stated in advance.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to any inferential claim only if the event count rises well above 11 and similarity beats a minutes-matched and a random-teammate baseline on held-out cases; otherwise report as descriptive and not supportive.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 (exclude earlier partial files).

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
What sample size and spell count are needed for a reliable test with only 11 cases?
How should initiation profile similarity and minutes or same-position minutes be measured without outcome leakage?
What confounders (injury type, role changes, regression to the mean) threaten attribution of gains after absence?
args.query: player absence offensive reorganization teammate with closest pre-absence initiation profile largest gainer in absent player's primary play types, 11 cases 148 spells

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
